verdict.rationale: The only container-related evidence is that Omarchy offers an easy way to run Windows through a Docker VM, installed via Install > Windows. This implies Docker is part of its tooling, but nothing confirms general-purpose container tools are preinstalled and ready with no setup. Development environments also go through an Install menu step rather than being present out of the box. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that Docker or other container tools ship preinstalled and configured, details on which container tooling is included (e.g. compose, lazydocker), and hands-on or independent corroboration of zero-setup container use.
